summary: Drawing inspiration from current and compelling space research, such as NASA's SPHEREx mission and the search for "Planet X," we have developed an academic website for middle and high school students that encourages the exploration of the unknown and the formulation of scientific theories. This platform aims to steer students away from the misinformation prevalent online, providing them with reliable and easily accessible information instead. At the same time, it seeks to bring our motto, "Question the universe. Explore the unknown," to life.
details: Inspired by current space exploration and astronomy, this project aims to provide middle and high school students with accessible, reliable, and academically grounded information. We have developed a website featuring five engaging main categories, each encompassing a variety of specific topics. Users can simply click on any subject that interests them to begin learning something new. By filtering out the overwhelming and often confusing clutter of information found online, this site connects students with credible and compelling content. The platform uses clear, straightforward language, enabling young researchers to develop their own ideas with ease. The website was built from scratch, manually coded using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript within Visual Studio Code. To ensure an engaging experience, the design is both cohesive and user-friendly. This was a collaborative team effort: the software architecture was developed by the team lead, while the research categories and topics were distributed among the team members. Throughout the process, we supported one another and took great care to use authoritative sources—such as NASA, ESA, and TUA—while strictly adhering to copyright standards. A complete list of the sources used can be found in the bibliography section of the website. We would like to thank the entire NASA Space Apps Challenge team for this invaluable experience, and we hope you enjoy exploring our platform!
